speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)

Based on the history of a late preterm infant (born at 32 weeks) delivered via cesarean section, the most likely diagnosis is Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn. The cesarean delivery likely bypassed the normal compression of the lungs during labor, leading to retained fetal lung fluid, while the gestational age is slightly older than the typical range for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), though mild surfactant deficiency cannot be entirely ruled out without further evaluation. Given the significant risk factors present, I would like to request an immediate Chest X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes such as pneumonia or meconium aspiration.
